report_sentences: **Title:** Gravity modulated by a reflectance×temperature interaction, and quadratic air drag that depends on shape, in a simulated drop and throw laboratory
Without air, flight time follows free fall, but the effective gravitational acceleration depends on the product reflectance×(temperature−20).

Next I ran replicate controlled objects (sphere, mass 1 kg, r 0.1 m, other properties fixed) and varied one factor at a time: shape, air density, mass, radius, and a 3×2 grid of temperature (−20, 20, 80) and reflectance (0, 0.5, 1) in a vacuum.
The model is: g_eff = 9.81 + 0.0625·(reflectance−0.5)·(temperature−20); drag acceleration = k·|v|·v with k = C_shape·ρ·r²/m.
At 20 °C, reflectance has no effect, and at reflectance 0.5, temperature has no effect.
Hot dark objects (80 °C, reflectance 0) fall slowly (t=1.60 s, g_eff≈7.9).
Hot white objects fall fast (t=1.31 s, g_eff≈11.7).
Cold dark objects fall fast (t=1.345 s) and cold white objects fall slowly (t=1.54 s).
- After the model fit, residuals show no significant trend in mass, radius, reflectance, temperature, stripes, hardness, batch, height or air density.
The first is an altered gravity that depends on the combination of reflectance and temperature.
- The g_eff form was fitted by eye, using the grid at only three temperatures and three reflectances, so nonlinearities are possible.
- Confidence is high for the existence of the reflectance×temperature and shape/density/size/mass effects.
